instrument_name: PA Personal Income Tax Guide - Income Subject to Tax Withholding (employer withholding chapter)
figure_or_rule_carried: Method: tax withheld = compensation subject to withholding x applicable rate for each payroll period; supplemental compensation is added to current-period compensation and multiplied by the rate; REV-419 nonwithholding certificate for reciprocal-state residents. Whole chapter text (120,252 chars, both segments) read: NO rounding rule for the income tax withholding amount. Flat rate 3.07% (Employer Withholding page, same session).
verification_method: webfetch-read 2026-10-29 (both text segments) | VERIFY 2026-10-29: mismatch — cited URL (chapter text, first 100k chars re-read) states no flat 3.07% rate, only "current applicable rate"; 3.07% not on this page

instrument_name: 61 Pa. Code 113.1 and 113.4 (Chapter 113 Withholding of Tax)
figure_or_rule_carried: Sections 113.1 (who must withhold) and 113.4 (filing and timing of statements) read: neither states a computation formula or a rounding rule. With US-PA-P5-2-001 and REV-415 (US-PA-009) the income tax rounding rule is absent from the statute-level and guide-level sources that would carry it.

instrument_name: PA L&I UC Tax: Employee Withholding (employee contribution and rounding rule)
authority: PA Department of Labor & Industry - Office of UC Tax Services
figure_or_rule_carried: UC employee contribution 0.07% (.0007) for 2023 and thereafter; calculations each payroll period carried to three decimals, excess dropped, rounded to the nearest whole cent (1.235-1.239 -> 1.24; 1.230-1.234 -> 1.23). Only rounding rule PA publishes for payroll withholding; it covers the UC employee contribution, not income tax.

instrument_name: Ohio Employer Withholding Taxes: Optional Computer Formula (Eff. Oct 1, 2025, Rev. 09/25)
figure_or_rule_carried: TW = (pay per period x PP) - (650 x exemptions); WD = TW x 0.01775 / PP if TW <= 26,050; ((TW-26,050) x 0.02990 + 462.39)/PP if 26,050 < TW <= 100,000; ((TW-100,000) x 0.03640 + 2,673.50)/PP above 100,000. The document has no rounding instruction. Together with the 2026 Filing Guidelines (zero hits, US-OH-P5-1-002) and the 2026 percentage-method PDF (no rounding text) the state withholding rounding rule is absent from the official computation documents. 2026 tables effective 2026-08-01 per US-OH-002.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 718.25 Rounding of amounts (municipal income tax)
figure_or_rule_carried: A person MAY round to the nearest whole dollar all amounts entered on any return, report, voucher or document under ch. 718 (50 cents and over up, under 50 cents dropped); if rounding, all amounts on the document are rounded. Optional; applies to municipal income tax documents.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 718.03 Withholding taxes from qualifying wages; 718.04 authority and rate limit
figure_or_rule_carried: 718.03: employer located or doing business in a taxing municipality withholds qualifying wages earned there x the municipality rate on the payment date; remits to the municipal tax administrator monthly (15 days after month-end) if prior-year withholding exceeded 2,399 USD or any month of the preceding quarter exceeded 200 USD, otherwise quarterly (last day of the month after the quarter); a municipality may require semimonthly if prior-year withholding exceeded 11,999 USD or a prior-year month exceeded 1,000 USD, and electronic payment. 718.04: uniform rate; no rate above 1% without elector approval, higher rates in force on 2015-03-23 grandfathered. 718.80 ff.: a net-profit taxpayer may elect the Tax Commissioner as sole administrator. Wage tax is administered by each municipality or its agent (CCA, RITA), not on the state withholding return.

instrument_name: Ohio IT 1040 booklet TY2025 - IT RC (resident credit) and IT NRC (nonresident credit) instructions
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident credit (IT RC): only for income taxed by another of the 50 states or DC on a return; not for states without an individual income tax; not for wages earned in IN, KY, MI, PA or WV while an Ohio resident (those states do not tax them under agreements with Ohio); city and foreign taxes excluded. Nonresident credit (IT NRC): part-year residents and nonresidents; compensation is Ohio-sourced if earned while resident or for services performed in Ohio, allocated by location of the specific services or the ratio of days worked in Ohio to total days worked (R.C. 5747.20). Employer withholding itself needs no credit computation. TY2025 booklet (TY2026 not read).

instrument_name: Ohio Declaration of Tax Representative, Form TBOR 1 (Rev. 11/23)
figure_or_rule_carried: TBOR 1: representative (attorney, CPA/PA, enrolled agent, officer, full-time employee, family member) per tax type, Ohio account number and period; may view returns, present evidence, object to audits, file petitions, waive limitation periods; does NOT authorize signing any form the Revised Code requires the taxpayer to sign; non-attorneys cannot sign voluntary disclosure or settlement agreements; valid up to three years, one year if no date is given. Part 1 taxpayer (FEIN), Part 2 representative and tax matters. ODJFS UI power of attorney (JFS 20107) still not opened from an official host (thesource.jfs.ohio.gov blocked in Chrome by domain-change check; jfs.ohio.gov form URL 404).

instrument_name: Ohio tax.ohio.gov Employer Withholding - Who Must Withhold (ORC 5747.06)
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer with an office or transacting business in Ohio withholds on residents and nonresidents; school district tax withheld for employees resident in a taxing district; withholding not required for residents of MI, IN, KY, WV or PA earning compensation for services in Ohio, nor for a nonresident civilian spouse of a servicemember stationed in Ohio. Confirms US-OH-P5-1-002.

instrument_name: MCL 206.703 Income Tax Act of 1967, Sec. 703 (tax withholding)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer required to withhold federally deducts tax = Sec. 51 rate x (compensation minus the pro-rata share of personal and dependency exemptions for the period); the Department may prescribe withholding tables. Full section (3 pages, compiled through PA 5 of 2025) read: no rounding rule. With Guide 446 TY2026 (zero hits, US-MI-P5-1-001) the rounding rule is absent from both statute and guide.

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury FAQ - Which cities impose an income tax?
figure_or_rule_carried: 24 Michigan cities levy income-related taxes (individual, withholding, corporate, partnership, fiduciary). Treasury administers Detroit only. The other 23 administer their own forms, filing, payment and taxpayer support: Albion, Battle Creek, Benton Harbor, Big Rapids, East Lansing, Grand Rapids, Flint, Grayling, Hamtramck, Highland Park, Hudson, Ionia, Jackson, Lansing, Lapeer, Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Pontiac, Port Huron, Portland, Saginaw, Springfield, Walker.

instrument_name: City Income Tax Act, Act 284 of 1964 - MCL 141.503 and 141.503a (rate ceilings)
figure_or_rule_carried: City ordinance incorporates the uniform city income tax ordinance and states the rate authorized by Sec. 11 of ch. 2, Sec. 3(2) or Secs. 3a-3c. City over 600,000 (Detroit): from 2013-01-01 max 2.40% residents, 1.20% nonresidents (2.20/1.10 once lighting-authority bonds are paid). Sec. 3a(2): city under 1,000,000 approved by electors before 1988-11-15 and meeting millage tests: max 2% residents, nonresidents not over 50% of the resident rate. Uniform rate (Sec. 11, ch. 2) not read this pass. Each city sets its rate by ordinance; individual city rates NOT read from city sources.

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury Form 151 Authorized Representative Declaration (Power of Attorney), Rev. 11-21
figure_or_rule_carried: Form 151 (PA 122 of 1941): representative may be an entity (individual contact required); Part 4 authority boxes: receive confidential information, make presentations, sign returns, enter into agreements, each restrictable by tax type and year; Part 5 copies of dispute notices (not city income tax); effective from signing unless a start date is set, until revoked unless an expiry date is set; taxpayer signs; FEIN, ME or TR number required for business taxes; filed by e-mail to Treas-Registration-151@michigan.gov or by mail.

UI POA: one form per representative (PEO, CPA, HR, bookkeeper, other service provider); general authorization = inspect confidential information, represent, sign quarterly or registration reports, enter into agreements, receive UIA mail, all years; or limited authorization (up to 4 boxes); employer FEIN and UIA account number; dates optional. MiUI also has a separate TPA authorization by TPA ID (UIA job aids; not opened).

instrument_name: O.C.G.A. 48-7-101 Collection of income tax at source; withholding (2025 Code of Georgia, Justia publication)
authority: Georgia General Assembly (text via Justia 2025 Code)
figure_or_rule_carried: Full section read: employers withhold a tax computed to approximate the annual liability by Commissioner regulation; standard-deduction and exemption allowances; bonuses per Commissioner rule (f)(5); employee exemption certificate (g); periodic and nonperiodic payments (h),(j); 6% Form 1099 backup (i). The section has NO 23-calendar-day exemption, NO nonresident threshold, NO reciprocity provision and no rounding rule. Mirror is not the official site (legis.ga.gov not reached): tier B.

instrument_name: O.C.G.A. Title 34 Ch. 7 Art. 1 Pt. 1 (Wages Generally, 34-7-1 to 34-7-5) incl. 34-7-2 full text
authority: Georgia General Assembly (text via Justia 2025 Code)
figure_or_rule_carried: Part 1 Wages Generally has five sections: 34-7-1 term of employment; 34-7-2 payment by money, check, payroll card or electronic transfer, at least two equal pay periods per month for covered employees, written explanation of payroll-card fees; 34-7-3 written instrument; 34-7-4 wages due a beneficiary; 34-7-5 redemption of checks. 34-7-2 read in full: payment form and frequency only. No itemized pay-statement duty in Part 1; Part 2 is PEOs (34-7-6). Record-keeping duty is O.C.G.A. 34-2-11 (cross reference, not read).

instrument_name: Georgia DOR 2026 Employer Withholding Tax Guide (rev. September 2026) - scan for 23-day, reciprocity, rounding, POA
figure_or_rule_carried: Full-text scan of the 2026 guide: no 23-calendar-day exemption, no reciprocity agreement, no rounding instruction (withholding by tables or percentage method; bonuses at the income tax rate, 5.19% before the 2026 rate change); third-party payroll provider without a client account number: client or a valid Power of Attorney may call 1-877-423-6711; providers with more than 250 employers must pay by EFT (O.C.G.A. 48-2-32). The 23-day figure seen in a search summary in round 1 is NOT supported by the statute (US-GA-P5-2-001) or the guide: unverified, do not use. Nonresident rule (5% or 5,000 USD) stands per US-GA-P5-1-001.
